display.purpose: The character inside a flap cell. Sized as a ratio of --c (x1.44), not as a fixed step, so the lead unit runs past a conventional display cap. Always tabular-nums, weight 700.

headline.purpose: The single line painted on the enamel wall below the board.

title.purpose: Caption under the lead (days) unit only; one step up from the other captions.

label.purpose: Rail key/value across the top of the board, and the departed-service line.

caption.purpose: Captions under small cell groups and the knob label.

shadows.name: board-recess
shadows.purpose: The board set into the wall. Containment ring, inset top falloff, bottom lip light, outside top edge light, short contact drop. Not a reusable card shadow.

shadows.name: leaf-upper-edge
shadows.purpose: Top highlight on the upper flap leaf.

shadows.name: leaf-lower-edge
shadows.purpose: Bottom shade on the lower flap leaf.

shadows.name: leaf-cast
shadows.value: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(0,0,0,.55), transparent) over the top 24% of the lower half
shadows.purpose: Shadow the descending leaf throws onto the half beneath, including onto its printed character.

shadows.name: hardware-seat
shadows.purpose: Screw heads and axle pins seated in their surface.

motion.name: flip-fall
motion.purpose: Descending leaf, rotateX 0 to -90deg, opacity cut at the last frame. Web Animations API, not CSS keyframes.

motion.name: flip-land
motion.purpose: Ascending leaf, rotateX 90deg to 0. On finish it writes the new character into the static lower half.

motion.name: roll-step
motion.purpose: Random glyph swap interval while a cell is spinning; 4-8 steps before the final value lands with a real flip.

motion.name: cascade-dest
motion.purpose: Left-to-right stagger across the two 13-cell destination rows.

motion.name: cascade-clock
motion.purpose: Clock cells land after the destination rows finish.

motion.name: knob-press
motion.purpose: Transform, box-shadow and colour on the enamel knob; removed entirely under reduced motion.

motion.name: blur-spin
motion.purpose: Spinning cell. Applied to the inner glyph, never the housing.

narrative.overview:
One piece of public hardware, photographed head-on. An institutional enamel wall fills the viewport and a dark split-flap board is recessed into it — not floating above it, set into it, with four screws at the corners and a lit top edge where the panel meets the paint. Every character on the board lives in a fixed cell with a visible housing and two axle pins; nothing on this surface is typeset, everything is mounted.

The system is committed to its palette rather than accented by it: the enamel green carries roughly half the visible surface, the board face carries the rest, bone is the only ink on the board, and a single signal red is reserved for one sentence. There is no third accent, no gradient brand mark, no soft neutral card. Density is tight and mechanical — 2–3px between cells, hairline rules of light rather than borders — while the countdown itself is deliberately enormous, past any usual display cap, because the number is the entire product.

The refusal is explicit and visible in the build: no centred neon digit block on a black field. Where a clock-face treatment would centre glowing numerals in void, this centres a timetable in a room.
keyCharacteristics: Two surfaces only: enamel wall, recessed board face.
Fixed character cells; text is padded with blank cells, never reflowed.
One typeface, all caps, all tracked, weights 400 and 700 only.
Depth is entirely inset — recess, bevel, hardware — with no floating elevation.
Every dimension of the mechanism derives from one custom property, --c.

rules.name: The Signal-For-Departed Rule
rules.body: Signal red states one thing only: a service that has already left. It is never a highlight, never a hover, never an error tint, never applied to a digit. If a new surface wants red for emphasis, it does not get red.

rules.name: The Two-Surface Rule
rules.body: There are exactly two backgrounds in this world: the enamel wall and the board face. New content either mounts onto the board or is painted on the wall. Inventing a third surface — a card, a panel, a tinted well — breaks the room.

rules.name: The Fixed Cell Rule
rules.body: Board text occupies a fixed number of character cells (destination lines are exactly 13). Shorter strings are centred by padding with blank cells; they never shrink the type, never recentre the row, never wrap.

rules.name: The All-Caps Signage Rule
rules.body: Every visible string is uppercase and tracked. Weight is 400 or 700 — nothing between, no italics, no third face.

rules.name: The --c Rule
rules.body: All cell geometry descends from a single per-unit custom property. --cell and --lead are the two source values; each unit assigns one of them to --c, and cell width, cell height, glyph size, axle-pin diameter and spin blur radius are all calc()ed from it. Changing a countdown's scale means changing one number, never a set of paired values.

rules.name: The Recess Rule
rules.body: New elements are inset or mounted. Outer box-shadow is limited to the board's containment ring and its short contact drop; no ambient card shadow, no glow, no lifted hover.

rules.name: The Fixed Housing Rule
rules.body: Motion blur is applied to the inner glyph element only, never to the flap itself. The housing is hardware: it does not blur, scale, or move. Only the character moves.

dos: Do derive every new mechanism dimension from --c with calc(), and set --c from --cell or --lead — never hard-code a cell width, glyph size, pin size or blur radius.
Do keep board text in fixed character cells, padded with blanks to the row width.
Do convey depth by insetting: recess, bevel, 1px light edge, contact drop.
Do apply motion blur to the inner glyph only; the housing is fixed hardware.
Do use Web Animations API for the flip so re-triggering cancels and restarts cleanly.
Do honour prefers-reduced-motion by removing blur and stopping the hundredths entirely rather than slowing them down.
Do ship type as self-hosted woff2 in fonts/, preloaded, font-display: swap.
Do treat the phone under 560px as the reference device: reflow to two units per row and raise --cell so digits stay large.
Do keep every string uppercase and tracked, at weight 400 or 700.
donts: Don't introduce a build step, a package manager, or any dependency. index.html, style.css, main.js and fonts/ are the whole system; anything needing package.json is out of this world by construction.
Don't cap the countdown at a conventional display size. The lead digits are meant to exceed 6rem; the number is the product.
Don't spend signal red on anything but a departed service.
Don't add a third surface colour, a second accent, or a second typeface.
Don't float anything: no ambient card shadows, no glow, no hover lift.
Don't let a countdown digit reflow the layout — tabular-nums is mandatory here.
Don't flip the hundredths. They swap under permanent blur; a leaf cannot fall at 100Hz and faking it reads as a stutter.
Don't replace the flip with CSS keyframes; a restarted keyframe animation mid-flight leaves a leaf stranded.
